status: RESEARCH OUTPUT — pure transcription of docs/fertilizer/knowledge-base.md; requires human review AND page-by-page primary re-verification before seeding cropRegistry.fertilizer
purpose: Fertilizer knowledge base for the 9 SPECIALIZED/GENERAL crops, transcribed from the verified-values table in docs/fertilizer/knowledge-base.md into the structure that same doc defines. Blanket (no-soil-test) recommendations only — no STCR soil-test tier is published anywhere in the repo.

rules.transcriptionOnly: Every number, unit, timing and source string in this file is literally written in docs/fertilizer/knowledge-base.md. Nothing is estimated, averaged, summed, converted or inferred. Values that are not written down are absent and listed in `gaps`.
rules.unitsExactlyAsPublished: The doc's own rule is quoted verbatim: 'no number without source.url; units stored exactly as published.' COTTON and WHEAT are per ACRE; the other seven are per hectare. NO unit normalisation was performed and none may be performed in the seed pipeline — docs/fertilizer/fertilizer-intelligence.md requires a 'unit-preservation test (per-acre sources never silently become per-ha)' and mandates that the display layer converts alongside the original.
rules.rangeValues: Where the source publishes a range in place of a single number (e.g. rice short-duration N '120–150'), the value is stored as a [min, max] array and the full published string is kept in `published`. No midpoint or average was computed.
rules.noSummedTotals: Where a crop has a blanket basal dose PLUS a separately published top-dress nitrogen figure (tomato, chilli, onion), `totalNpk` holds the basal dose EXACTLY as published and the top-dress appears only in `schedule`. The source publishes no summed season total, so none was computed.
rules.i18nKeys: `fractionKey` and `symptomKey` are i18n key strings, never display text — the API never returns display language text (docs/api/error-codes.md). The keys in this file are NEWLY MINTED here; no en/hi strings exist for them yet (gap F15). The exact published wording each key must render is preserved in the sibling `note`.
rules.fractionKeyNamespace: fertilizer.schedule.basal.* for at-planting applications, fertilizer.schedule.split.* for splits whose proportion the source does not state, fertilizer.schedule.topdress.* for later applications. A key ending in `unspecifiedFraction` means the source names the application but publishes no proportion for it.
rules.unitNote: `totalNpk.unitNote` records how the unit was determined from the published row — including the rows where the unit is NOT written at all (onion) or where only the area denominator is written (cotton, wheat).
rules.accessedSemantics: `accessed: 2026-08-12` on every source object is the date docs/fertilizer/knowledge-base.md records for its research ('Verified values (as researched 2026-08-12)'). These external pages were NOT re-fetched for this file; it was transcribed from the repo doc on 2026-08-13. The doc's own instruction stands: 're-verify page-by-page during seed authoring'.
rules.verificationPending: Set true wherever docs/fertilizer/knowledge-base.md marks the row ⚠️ in its Status column: potato (region flag — plains value missing), soybean (bulletin PDF citation missing), wheat (PAU value not verified against the PDF). docs/fertilizer/fertilizer-intelligence.md: 'KB entries marked verificationPending: true until done — UI shows source anyway'.

gaps.field: organics[].unit and micronutrients[].unit — every organic and micronutrient figure
gaps.problem: docs/fertilizer/knowledge-base.md writes the NPK doses with an explicit unit but writes the organic and micronutrient quantities as bare numbers: tomato 'FYM 25t ... borax 10 + ZnSO₄ 50', potato 'MgSO₄ 60', soybean 'FYM 5–10t', onion Bellary 'ZnSO₄ 50'. No per-area denominator is written for any of them, and for FYM even the tonnes have no denominator.
gaps.checked: docs/fertilizer/knowledge-base.md (the whole Verified-values table), docs/fertilizer/fertilizer-intelligence.md. No unit is stated anywhere in the repo.
gaps.impact: These figures cannot be rendered to a farmer without a unit. Assuming t/ha and kg/ha is almost certainly right agronomically — which is exactly why assuming it is dangerous: it would be an unsourced number wearing a citation.
gaps.resolution: `unit: null` everywhere, with the bare published string preserved in `published`. Units must be read off the TNAU PDFs during seed authoring.

gaps.problem: The only potato entry is 'Potato (TN hills)'. The doc's Status cell reads '⚠️ region flag: add PAU/UP value for plains before demo in northern persona'. Meanwhile docs/crop-recommendation/scoring-model.md characterises potato as 'Rabi (plains)', and docs/crop-recommendation/engine.md scopes the demo to MP/Maharashtra/UP — i.e. plains states.
gaps.checked: docs/fertilizer/knowledge-base.md, docs/fertilizer/fertilizer-intelligence.md ('Regional variance (TNAU potato ≠ Punjab potato — flagged per-entry; ship with stated region context)'), docs/crop-recommendation/scoring-model.md.
gaps.impact: A northern-plains demo persona would be shown a TN-hills dose (120:240:120 kg/ha) as its potato guidance. The 240 kg/ha P2O5 figure in particular is a hills-specific value.
gaps.resolution: verificationPending: true, and context.region is stated explicitly as 'Tamil Nadu (TN) — hills'. A PAU/UP plains recommendation must be added as a second entry before a northern-persona demo.

gaps.checked: docs/fertilizer/knowledge-base.md, docs/fertilizer/fertilizer-intelligence.md, docs/i18n/agricultural-terminology.md (its Diseases table has no nutrient-deficiency entries).

gaps.field: schedule[].fractionKey — nutrient scope of the split is unstated for COTTON and POTATO
gaps.problem: Cotton is published as 'varieties 50/50 basal & 40–45 DAS' and 'hybrids thirds basal/40–45/60–65 DAS'; potato as 'half basal/half 30 DAS'. None of these says whether the split applies to nitrogen only or to the whole NPK dose. Phosphorus is normally applied wholly basal (as the rice row explicitly states, 'P basal'), which makes a whole-dose reading doubtful — but the source does not say.
gaps.checked: docs/fertilizer/knowledge-base.md Schedule-core column for all 9 rows.
gaps.impact: A wrong reading changes the P and K timing for three of the nine crops.
gaps.resolution: Neutral keys (…halfDose / …thirdDose) with the ambiguity recorded in every affected schedule note. Resolve from the TNAU pages during seed authoring.

gaps.field: WHEAT schedule — urea quantity across two irrigations
gaps.problem: Published as 'urea 45kg before 1st & 2nd irrigation'. It is not stated whether that is 45 kg BEFORE EACH irrigation (90 kg total) or 45 kg split across the two.
gaps.impact: A factor-of-two difference in the top-dressed nitrogen for wheat.
gaps.resolution: Two schedule entries created (one per irrigation) with the identical published string and the ambiguity flagged in both notes; no quantity was assigned to either entry. This is part of the row's existing ⚠️ verification task.

gaps.field: ONION — the row publishes NO unit
gaps.problem: Every other TNAU-sourced row writes kg/ha explicitly. The onion row ('small: 30:60:30 basal +30 N @30 DAS; Bellary: 50:150:75 basal +50 N @30 DAP + ZnSO₄ 50') writes no unit anywhere.
gaps.checked: docs/fertilizer/knowledge-base.md onion row, compared against the rice/maize/tomato/potato/chilli rows.
gaps.impact: Onion is the designated 'star mandi demo' crop (docs/product/crop-support-matrix.md), so its guidance card is likely to be shown live. An unlabelled dose must never reach a farmer.
gaps.resolution: unit: null for both onion recommendations, with unitNote explaining why it was not assumed. Almost certainly kg/ha from the same TNAU PDF — but 'almost certainly' is not a source.

gaps.field: ONION Bellary schedule — '30 DAP' vs '30 DAS'
gaps.problem: The Bellary entry reads '+50 N @30 DAP' while the sibling small-onion entry reads '+30 N @30 DAS' for the same 30-day timing. 'DAP' is simultaneously a common abbreviation for days-after-planting and the name of a fertiliser (di-ammonium phosphate) that appears elsewhere in this very doc (wheat: 'DAP 55kg sowing').
gaps.impact: Low agronomic impact (both readings put the top-dress at 30 days) but a real i18n/display hazard if 'DAP' is rendered literally to a farmer next to a nitrogen dose.
gaps.resolution: Transcribed exactly as written ('30 DAP') with the ambiguity recorded in the schedule note. Not silently normalised to DAS.

gaps.field: totalNpk — no season totals for TOMATO, CHILLI, ONION
gaps.problem: These three publish a basal NPK dose plus one or more separate absolute top-dress nitrogen figures (tomato +75 N @30d; chilli +30 N @30/60/90d; onion small +30 N @30 DAS, Bellary +50 N @30 DAP). The source never publishes the summed season nitrogen.
gaps.checked: docs/fertilizer/knowledge-base.md rows for tomato, chilli, onion.
gaps.impact: totalNpk is therefore NOT a season total for these three crops — it is the published basal dose. A consumer that reads totalNpk as 'the season dose' will understate nitrogen (tomato by 75, chilli by 90, per the published units).
gaps.resolution: No addition performed. The field name comes from the structure the doc itself defines; the discrepancy is recorded here and in each schedule note. A reviewer should decide whether the structure needs a distinct `basalNpk` vs `seasonTotalNpk` distinction — that is a schema change requiring approval.

gaps.field: structure — no field for secondary nutrients (S, Mg)
gaps.problem: The structure defined by docs/fertilizer/knowledge-base.md provides totalNpk, organics and micronutrients only. Soybean publishes 'S 20 kg/ha' and potato publishes 'MgSO₄ 60'; sulphur and magnesium are secondary nutrients, not micronutrients.
gaps.impact: Both values are currently filed under `micronutrients`, which mislabels them.
gaps.resolution: Recorded under micronutrients with an explicit note on each. Adding a secondaryNutrients field would change the documented structure and needs approval.

gaps.field: context.region — not published for MAIZE, SOYBEAN, ONION, CHILLI, WHEAT
gaps.problem: Four rows are labelled with a region in parentheses (rice 'TN, transplanted', tomato 'TN', potato 'TN hills', cotton 'TN'); five are not. Wheat's region is implied only by its source being PAU (Punjab).
gaps.impact: docs/fertilizer/fertilizer-intelligence.md requires the guidance to 'ship with stated region context' and to be labeled 'General recommendation (no soil test) — Source: TNAU/PAU/ICAR'. Five crops currently have no region string to display.
gaps.resolution: region: null where not published, with the source organisation recorded in the context note so the reviewer can supply it deliberately. Not inferred from the source organisation.

gaps.problem: The disclaimer is required on every fertilizer surface in BOTH en and hi. Only the English text is written in the repo.
gaps.checked: docs/fertilizer/knowledge-base.md Disclaimer section; docs/i18n/agricultural-terminology.md (has term-level Hindi but no sentence-level disclaimer); docs/i18n/translation-strategy.md not consulted for content (it defines process, not strings).
gaps.impact: The hi rendering of a legally/ethically load-bearing disclaimer does not exist.
gaps.resolution: hi: null. NOT machine-translated — CLAUDE.md rule 8 requires human verification of agronomic Hindi, and docs/i18n/agricultural-terminology.md notes that the UI must use full sentence keys rather than concatenated fragments.

gaps.field: basis — no STCR / soil-test tier exists
gaps.problem: The structure defines basis as 'blanket_no_soil_test' | 'stcr_soil_test', and docs/fertilizer/fertilizer-intelligence.md states that every SAU publishes both tiers ('blanket dose ... + STCR soil-test dose — so our KB mirrors it'). No STCR values are published in the repo for any crop.
gaps.impact: None immediately — fertilizer-intelligence.md defers the soil-test tier to P3 ('Soil-test values present (P3 upload): defer to the card, don't recompute'). Recorded so the empty half of the enum is not mistaken for missing transcription.
gaps.resolution: Every recommendation in this file is basis: 'blanket_no_soil_test'. Wheat's '(medium fertility)' is a fertility CONDITION on a blanket dose, not an STCR dose, and is recorded in context.condition.

gaps.field: schedule — no schedule published for WHEAT nutrient dose, and no timings in days for RICE
gaps.problem: Wheat's Schedule-core cell says only 'as stated' and the schedule information that exists is expressed in fertiliser PRODUCTS (DAP/urea), not in fractions of the 50 N + 25 P2O5 nutrient dose. Rice's four N&K splits are named by growth stage (basal/tillering/PI/heading) with no days-after-transplanting figures and no per-split proportion.
gaps.impact: docs/fertilizer/fertilizer-intelligence.md's product is 'stage-driven guidance cards: what nutrient matters now, when to apply'. 'When' cannot be computed for rice from stage names alone unless the crop's stage model (crops.agronomy.json kcStages) supplies the day offsets — a cross-file join that nothing in the repo currently authorises.
gaps.resolution: timing: null wherever no timing is published; fraction keys ending 'unspecifiedFraction' wherever no proportion is published. No day numbers were borrowed from crops.agronomy.json.

gaps.field: whole file — values are second-hand and dated
gaps.problem: docs/fertilizer/knowledge-base.md heads its table 'Verified values (as researched 2026-08-12 — re-verify page-by-page during seed authoring)' and docs/fertilizer/fertilizer-intelligence.md records the basis as a 'subagent report 2026-08-12'. No source page was fetched for this transcription.
gaps.impact: Every number here is a transcription of a transcription. The doc's own instruction to re-verify page-by-page is unfulfilled for all 9 crops, not only the three marked ⚠️.
gaps.resolution: source.accessed is recorded as 2026-08-12 (the research date the doc states), never as today, so the age of the evidence is visible. Page-by-page re-verification remains a prerequisite for seeding.
